summary: Catherine Bell (1954–2008) was a scholar in religious studies and sinology. She studied under Joseph Kitagawa at the University of Chicago and served as the Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University from 1985 to 2008.

Catherine Cornille is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied at KU Leuven and the University of Hawaiʻi. Around 2004, she held a post as Associate Professor of Comparative Theology at Boston College.

Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher (1946–2023) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She earned her PhD from the University of Minnesota by 1984, where she also served as an Assistant Professor from circa 1983 to 2021.

Catherine Ludvik specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto under David B. Waterhouse, also studying with Antonino Forte and Werner Knobl, and held posts at Hanazono University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Catherine Prueitt works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She earned her BA from the University of Rochester and her PhD from Emory University under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton, later becoming an Assistant Professor at the University of British Columbia.
Cathy Cantwell works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Kent in 1989 and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall (1856–1906) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge, Oxford, and under Edward Byles Cowell and Theodor Benfey, he held posts at the British Museum, British Library, University College London, and Cambridge.

Cecil Y. Lang (1920–2003) studied at Duke University from circa 1937 to 1941. He held academic posts at Yale University, the University of Chicago, and the University of Virginia, where he served as Professor of English from circa 1970 to 1991.

Chack-fan Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Western Ontario. He served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.
Chaesong Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Kim pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo, attested in 1995, and studied under Yasunori Ejima.

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche (1930–2002) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Delog Dawa Drolma, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, Jangchub Dorje, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Chaim Rabin (1915–1996) was a linguist who studied at SOAS University of London and the University of Oxford. He held academic posts at the University of Oxford from 1941 to 1956 and at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from 1956 to 1986.

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held research posts at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and served as Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago, attested in 2015.

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, holding a doctorate from the University of Oxford. He held posts at Clare Hall, Cambridge, Trinity College, Oxford, and National University of Singapore, before becoming a Distinguished Professor at Lancaster University.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit works in Buddhist studies and religious studies, holding a BA from Chulalongkorn University. In 2012, he was attested as a Professor at Kasetsart University and a part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University.
Champa Thupten Zongtse is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen, where he was attested in 1991 and served as a Lecturer in 2009.

Chan Ju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and studied at the University of Tokyo. His teachers and supervisors included Charles Hallisey, John D. Dunne, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda.
Chandima is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under the instruction of Uma Shankar Vyas.

Chandrabhāl Tripathi (1929–1996) was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Göttingen and the University of Cologne, later serving as Professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin.

Chang-geun Hwang specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 2000, having studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.
